unit.name: Deep Q-learning and bootstrapped targets
unit.description: Explains how a neural network approximates Q-values, how targets are computed from the network itself, and how Q-learning updates the network.
unit.summary: Deep Q-learning replaces a memory-heavy Q-table with a neural Q-function, using a forward pass to estimate action values from a state [ts=2136s] [ts=2161s]. For the toy example, a one-hot encoded state is fed to a network whose output layer has one Q-value per action; more actions would require more output neurons [ts=2187s] [ts=2216s]. The training target is bootstrapped from immediate reward plus discounted maximum Q-value at the next state, while that target is held fixed for the current backpropagation step [ts=2476s] [ts=2524s]. The vanilla DQN loop initializes the Q-network, loops through episodes and time steps, selects the action with maximum Q-value, observes reward and next state, computes the target/loss, and updates parameters with gradient descent [ts=3107s] [ts=3163s].

key_points.text: Deep Q-learning uses a neural network as a Q-function so it can approximate action values without storing every state-action entry in a table.
The Q-network can map an encoded state to multiple outputs, one per available action, such as Q(s,right) and Q(s,left).
For DQN training, the target value y is computed as immediate reward plus gamma times the maximum Q-value at the next state.
During backpropagation, the bootstrapped target is held fixed so the update changes the current Q estimate toward that target.
The DQN training loop uses episodes, time steps, forward propagation, greedy action choice, observed reward/next state, target computation, loss, and gradient descent.

kp_catalog.name: Bellman optimality equation
kp_catalog.description: The recursive condition relating optimal Q-value to immediate reward plus discounted best future Q-value.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Bellman optimality is the core prerequisite relation behind DQN targets and value-based RL.

kp_catalog.name: Neural Q-function approximation
kp_catalog.description: Using a neural network to approximate Q(s,a) when tabular Q-learning is infeasible for large state/action spaces.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Neural Q-function approximation supports DQN after Bellman targets are established.

kp_catalog.name: DQN target, loss, and gradient update
kp_catalog.description: Bootstrapped training of a Q-network using y = r + gamma max Q(s',a') as a target and regression loss against Q(s,a).
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The DQN target, loss, and update rule are the main technical bridge from tabular RL to deep RL.
